title: How Russia Sees the World Now
gist: Teaser of Dmitry Adamsky's essay: nearly five years into the Ukraine war and 22 months into Trump's second term, Russia's strategic 'mental map' has shifted, starting with seeing Europe rather than the United States as its principal adversary; the text is truncated by a paywall.

insights.claim: In 2022 the Kremlin viewed the United States as its principal rival, saw Europe and NATO largely as extensions of American power, and treated nuclear muscle-flexing as an efficient coercive tool.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Baseline against which the author argues Russian strategy has since changed.
insights.locator: In 2022, when Russia launched its full-scale war

insights.claim: After nearly five years of war and 22 months of the second Trump administration, the mental map guiding Russian strategy has changed, and Russia now sees Europe, rather than the United States, as its main adversary (the text cuts off at this point).
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Suggests Russian pressure and escalation risk are increasingly directed at Europe.
insights.quote: First, Russia now sees Europe, instead of the United States, as
insights.locator: Today, after nearly five years of war
